description:
FOUND s495e (task #2099; everyday/idioms/list-util.pl).

    use List::Util qw(pairs);
    my @all = pairs(1..4);  print ref($all[-1]);        perl List::Util::_Pair   PCL ARRAY
    my $s   = pairs(1..4);  print "'$s' ", ref($s);     perl 'List::Util::_Pair=ARRAY(0x..)' List::Util::_Pair
                                                        PCL  '2' (the COUNT), ref ""

The generic rule is RIGHT -- a plain list-returning sub in scalar context yields its LAST
element under PCL as under perl (probe scratch/s495e/p-misc2.pl 'lastlist': `sub refs { ([1],[2]) }`
gives ref ARRAY on both).  So this is specific to how `pairs` is provided.

LAYER (CLAUDE.md 9a): List::Util is a MODULE, so this is `lib/List/Util.pm` -- `pairs` should
build objects blessed into List::Util::_Pair (perl's own class, with `key` and `value` methods
reading elements 0 and 1) and return a LIST, so scalar context falls out of the language rule.
The sibling `pairmap`/`pairgrep`/`pairkeys`/`pairvalues`/`unpairs` should be checked in the
same pass, and `List::Util::_Pair`'s own `->key`/`->value` are what everyday code calls.

ACCEPTANCE: the two probe lines above identical to perl; everyday/idioms/list-util.pl becomes
`same` (its baseline row leaves BY EDIT).


=== DONE (s495f, 2026-09-25) ===
lib/List/Util.pm (shim layer): `pairs` blesses each [k, v] into List::Util::_Pair (package added at the end of the shim with key / value / TO_JSON, List::Util's own names); an odd list pads the last pair with undef.  pairs / unpairs / pairkeys / pairvalues now answer the LAST element in scalar context (`wantarray ? @out : $out[-1]`) -- the real ones are XS list returners (probed: scalar(pairkeys(a=>1,b=>2,c=>3)) is "c", scalar(unpairs([5,6],[7,9])) is 9); `return @out` answered the count.  unpairs contributes exactly TWO elements per ref, undef-padded (perl: unpairs([1,2],[3]) is 1,2,3,undef; the shim's `map { @$_ }` dropped the undef).  pairmap (element count) and pairgrep (pair count) scalar rules unchanged and guarded.  The "Odd number of elements in pairs" warning is warnings-gated in perl (category misc) and stays absent like the rest of that family (not-supported.md "Warnings-gated diagnostics are absent", #221).
Probe table scratch/s495f/p-pairs.pl (22 lines incl. deref/write-through, sort by ->value, stringification `List::Util::_Pair=ARRAY(0x..)`, TO_JSON) identical to perl.
Guard: Pl/t/transpile-test-09.t last row (differential), inverse-verified on a 3d9b3712 extraction.  everyday idioms/list-util -> same (row edited out).
subject: SILENT WRONG (List::Util): `pairs` returns plain ARRAY refs instead of blessed List::Util::_Pair objects (so ->key / ->value do not exist), and in SCALAR context it answers the COUNT where perl answers the last pair
